contract.title: Conical CD nozzle, r_e = 35.4 mm, p0 = 200 kPa
contract.requested_prompt: Simulate the converging-diverging nozzle and compare with quasi-1-D theory.

objectives.description: Settled, conservative solution consistent with quasi-1-D theory.

checks.rationale: Normal exit at the requested horizon.
No genuine fatal signature in solver logs.
checkMesh reports Mesh OK.
Executed case equals the frozen case.
p, T, rho positive at every step.
No NaN/Inf in saved states.
maxCo 0.4 controller target with 2 % tolerance.
A zero-gradient outlet is only admissible if every outlet face is supersonic.
Reservoir inflow must be subsonic.
No reverse flow at inlet.
Inlet faces reproduce the total pressure.
Inlet faces reproduce the total temperature.
Choked throat band.
Exit static pressure exceeds nominal ambient (regime assessment only).
Diverging section remains supersonic.
Storage-aware discrete mass balance (0.01 %).
Restarts continue the checkpoint.
Adiabatic inviscid flow conserves stagnation enthalpy (5 % screen).
Face rho U.S agrees with the solver's numerical flux.
Quasi-1-D exit pressure screening bound for a finite-angle conical nozzle.
Quasi-1-D exit Mach, T, U, and mass-flow screening bound.
The frozen 6 ms horizon must be reached.
The 2 ms stationarity window must be available.
Inlet and outlet mass flow agree within 0.1 % over the window.
Per-step monitors drift < 0.2 % over the window.
Exit and throat states drift < 0.2 % over the window.
Relative L2 field change < 0.2 % over the window.

assumptions.justification: Regime assessment only; not imposed at outlet.

limitations: Single-mesh verification of an inviscid axisymmetric wedge.
Quasi-1-D tolerances are screening bounds, not validation.
